$comment: Executable receipts for the numbers coding-agent-internals publishes in prose - the page and table counts on the README's first screen and in index.html's JSON-LD, the shape of the twelve agent pages, the benchmark helper scripts, and the star snapshots the pages pin. Every figure that can be recomputed from committed data carries a `check.cmd`; every figure quoted from an upstream project carries `check.manual` with the upstream URL in the reason, because no file in this repository derives it and a check must run offline. Run with `python3 -m verify_claims --root . run`; CI runs it via .github/workflows/claims.yml. Note what this file is not: the benchmark result tables stay 预期结果 (hypotheses, not measurements) and are listed under `benchmark-expected-results` as manual - nothing here claims a measured number of this project's own.

claims.method: Ten of the twelve pages are the eight terminal CLIs of the main matrix plus Cursor and Windsurf; Cline and Devin complete the set. The same twelve names appear in the README's Agent Cards table, in index.html's agent grid and as SoftwareApplication entries in its JSON-LD.

claims.claim: The dimension pages carry the mechanism levels the catalogue publishes: three Level headings each in search, editing and security, four sub-agent patterns (A-D), and the memory page's four states - the three published levels plus the 中间态 compaction middle state.

claims.claim: sitemap.xml parses and lists 18 URLs - the site root, the five dimension pages and the twelve agent pages - each resolving to a committed .md page.
claims.metric: loc entries in sitemap.xml vs the committed page files
claims.method: The sitemap lists the .html rendered form; every slug it names is checked against the committed agents/ and dimensions/ Markdown, so a page cannot be dropped or renamed without the sitemap failing. Parsing the file also proves it is well-formed XML, which is one of this repository's two structural gates.

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import os,xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
ns='{http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9}'
base='https://alloevil.github.io/coding-agent-internals/'
locs=[e.text for e in ET.parse('sitemap.xml').iter(ns+'loc')]
md=lambda u: u[len(base):].replace('.html','.md')
missing=[u for u in locs if u!=base and not os.path.exists(md(u))]
slugs=sorted(md(u) for u in locs if u!=base)
files=sorted('agents/'+f for f in os.listdir('agents'))+sorted('dimensions/'+f for f in os.listdir('dimensions'))
print(len(locs),'urls; missing:',(','.join(missing) or 'none'),'; slugs match committed pages:',slugs==files)"

expect.equals: 18 urls; missing: none ; slugs match committed pages: True

claims.claim: The three star figures the site prints are the snapshots the agent pages pin: index.html's cards show 30.7K / 244.5K / 107K, exactly the rounded 30,667 / 244,530 / 106,920 the omp, Hermes and Gemini CLI pages record as a 2026-09-12 GitHub API reading, and the page footer carries the same date.
claims.metric: the `Stars` row of the three agent pages vs the agent-card labels and footer of index.html
claims.method: Each agent page pins its precise count and read date; index.html abbreviates them. The check re-does the abbreviation (within 0.1K) and requires the same date in the footer, so the two surfaces can no longer disagree about one snapshot. Whether that snapshot still matches the live repository is a separate, manual claim per agent.
claims.evidence: agents/omp.md, agents/hermes.md, agents/gemini-cli.md (Stars rows); index.html (agent cards, footer)

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import re
idx=open('index.html',encoding='utf-8').read()
foot=re.search(r'Last updated: (\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d)',idx).group(1)
out=[]
for p in ('agents/omp.md','agents/hermes.md','agents/gemini-cli.md'):
    t=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
    m=re.search(r'Stars \| ([\d.]+)K（([\d,]+)，(\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d)',t)
    k,n,d=m.groups()
    ok=(k+'K ⭐') in idx and abs(round(int(n.replace(',',''))/1000,1)-float(k))<=0.11 and d==foot
    out.append(p.split('/')[-1]+'='+k+'K('+n+','+d+')'+(' pinned' if ok else ' MISMATCH'))
print('; '.join(out)+'; footer '+foot)"

claims.claim: search-bench.sh takes the two documented positional arguments - a target directory and a search term - and runs offline: given a local directory it measures a cold search and ten consecutive searches for both a fixed string and a regex, using rg when present and falling back to grep.

T=$(mktemp -d) && printf 'const x = 1; // useSyncExternalStore probe
' > "$T/a.ts" && cd benchmarks && ./search-bench.sh "$T" useSyncExternalStore; rc=$?; rm -rf "$T"; exit $rc
